title: UNDERSTANDING STROKE: CAUSES, WARNING SIGNS AND PREVENTION
nextLesson: HOW DOES YOUR BODY RECOVER AFTER A STROKE?

o: A disease that only affects the heart
Blood flow to part of the brain is cut off, or a vessel in the brain bleeds
A problem caused only by old age
A pain in the neck muscles
questions.good: Correct! A stroke is a blocked or burst vessel that harms brain cells.
questions.hint: Think about what the brain needs to survive.
questions.review: What a stroke is: a blocked or burst vessel in the brain.

o: About one hundredth
About one tenth
About one fifth
About one half
questions.q: About how much of the body's oxygen does the brain use?
questions.good: Exactly! The brain is small but uses about one fifth of the body's oxygen.
questions.hint: The brain is only two percent of body weight, yet it is very hungry.
questions.review: Why the brain needs a constant blood supply.

o: Hemorrhagic stroke
Ischemic stroke
Both are equally common
Neither, because strokes are rare
questions.q: Which type of stroke is the most common?
questions.good: Correct! About eighty-five in every hundred strokes are ischemic.
questions.hint: It is the type caused by a blockage.
questions.review: The two types of stroke and which is more common.

o: The clot stays in the heart forever
The clot dissolves before it moves
The clot travels in the blood to the brain and blocks an artery
The clot makes the arteries wider
questions.q: How does a clot from the heart cause a stroke in atrial fibrillation?
questions.good: Right! This is called an embolism.
questions.hint: The word embolism means a clot that travels.

o: A harmless event that needs no action
A short blockage whose symptoms go away, but which is a serious warning
A stroke that only affects the legs
A type of headache
questions.q: What is a transient ischemic attack, or mini-stroke?
questions.good: Correct! The symptoms vanish, but you must still seek help at once.
questions.hint: The symptoms pass, but the danger does not.
questions.review: Transient ischemic attack as a serious warning.

o: The part of the brain that controls speech
The dead core of the stroke
Damaged tissue around the core that can still be saved
The skull bone
questions.good: Excellent! Fast treatment protects the penumbra.
questions.hint: It surrounds the core and can still recover.
questions.review: Core, penumbra and why time matters.

o: High blood pressure
Drinking enough water
Sleeping eight hours
Being left-handed
questions.q: Which is the biggest risk factor for stroke?
questions.good: Correct! High blood pressure damages and weakens the arteries.
questions.hint: It often has no symptoms and harms the artery walls.
questions.review: High blood pressure as the number one risk factor.

o: Take a tablet
Think about it for an hour
Try to walk it off
Call emergency services immediately and note the time
questions.q: In the word FAST, what does the letter T tell you to do?
questions.good: Right! Time is brain, and every minute counts.
questions.review: The FAST warning signs and calling for help at once.

o: Note the time the symptoms began
Give the person food, drink, or medicine
Stay with the person
Call emergency services
questions.q: While waiting for the ambulance, what should you NOT do?
questions.good: Correct! Doctors must first find out the type of stroke.
questions.hint: The treatments for a clot and for bleeding are opposite.
questions.review: What to do, and what not to do, in a suspected stroke.

o: Adding extra salt to every meal
Staying inactive
Ignoring high blood pressure
Controlling blood pressure, eating well, moving daily, and not smoking
questions.good: Excellent! These steps cut your risk year after year.
questions.hint: Think about the five prevention steps in the lesson.
questions.review: The prevention steps: pressure, food, exercise, smoking, and treating causes.

announcements.text: Write down the four FAST signs and teach them to one person at home.
